claim_verdicts.evidence: Claim text now names the per-iteration call, which is what makes 8 correct. Re-confirmed today on donhang-db: `select customer_id, count(*) from orders group by customer_id` returns `1|7`. The loop version itself cannot be re-run (never committed; repo clean at stage-1), but EF Core docs settle the per-iteration behaviour: "EF Core always executes a LINQ query on a DbSet against the database and only returns results based on what is in the database." 7 x FirstOrDefaultAsync + 1 for the orders = 8.

Re-ran live today with the lesson's own Try it commands: log_statement='all', login as anh.tran@example.com, GET /api/v1/orders -> HTTP 200, 7 entries. donhang-db logged exactly one statement for that call: "execute <unnamed>: SELECT o.id, o.customer_id, o.placed_at, o.status, c.id, c.city, c.email, c.full_name, c.password_hash / FROM orders AS o / INNER JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.id / WHERE o.customer_id = $1 / ORDER BY o.id". log_statement reset to 'none' (SHOW confirms).

claim_verdicts.evidence: Unchanged since round 1. efficient-querying.md, "Beware of lazy loading": "each iteration in the inner foreach triggers an additional database query, in its own roundtrip. As a result, after the initial query loading all the blogs, we then have another query *per blog*... this is sometimes called the *N+1* problem"; and "Because lazy loading makes it extremely easy to inadvertently trigger the N+1 problem, it is recommended to avoid it. Eager or explicit loading make it very clear in the source code when a database roundtrip occurs."

`git show stage-1:DonHang.Infrastructure/EfOrderRepository.cs` lines 9-14 are character-for-character the lesson's first code block: FindAsync = `db.Orders.Include(o => o.Items).FirstOrDefaultAsync(o => o.Id == id)`; ListByCustomerAsync = `db.Orders.Where(o => o.CustomerId == customerId).Include(o => o.Customer).OrderBy(o => o.Id).ToListAsync()`. One Include each.

`git show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Controllers/OrdersController.cs | cat -n` shows lines 48-56 matching the quoted block exactly, comment line included: `[Authorize]`, `[HttpGet]`, `int.Parse(User.FindFirstValue(JwtRegisteredClaimNames.Sub)!)`, `repository.ListByCustomerAsync(customerId)`, `orders.Select(o => new OrderSummaryDto(o.Id, o.Status, o.Customer!.FullName)).ToList()`. Live GET http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders returned `customerName` per entry, confirming the route and the projection.

Reworded text is now fully supported. No lazy loading anywhere at stage-1: only `services.AddDbContext<DonHangDbContext>(options => options.UseNpgsql(connectionString))`, no proxies package, and `Order`/`Customer` are `sealed` with non-virtual navigations. Fix-up clause: "Entity Framework Core will automatically fix-up navigation properties to any other entities that were previously loaded into the context instance." "Same request" is right because AddDbContext "registers DbContext types with a scoped lifetime by default".

New claim, and the docs state it flatly: "When working against relational databases, EF loads related entities by introducing JOINs into a single query" and "EF Core uses single query mode by default in the absence of any configuration." No `AsSplitQuery` / `UseQuerySplittingBehavior` anywhere at stage-1. Confirmed live: the one logged statement for GET /api/v1/orders is a single `INNER JOIN customers` query.

Ran it live: EF Core's statement is logged over five lines and grep prints only the first, so the learner sees `execute <unnamed>: SELECT c.id, c.city, ...` (the login) and `execute <unnamed>: SELECT o.id, o.customer_id, ...` (this call) — the words `FROM orders AS o` are on a continuation line grep drops. issues.text: The colon makes the sentence claim that `customerId` and `[Authorize]` ARE the last two lines of the method. They are not: `[Authorize]` is an attribute above the signature (line 49 of the file) and `var customerId = ...` is line 53; the last two lines are `var orders = await repository.ListByCustomerAsync(customerId);` and the `return Ok(orders.Select(...))`. As written the pointer sends the reader to the wrong lines — the two named are exactly the ones that do not matter.
issues.fix: Split the two halves: "Only the last two lines of the method matter for that — the repository call and the `.Select(...)` that builds the response. The two things above them are just context: `customerId` identifies the signed-in customer and `[Authorize]` keeps the endpoint closed to strangers; neither changes how many queries run."

issues.text: Before you start tells me I already know "a query built with LINQ", but the only prerequisite listed is saving-changes, whose five lines are about AddAsync, SaveChangesAsync, one transaction and generated ids - nothing about LINQ or about when a query runs. LINQ then carries the Core concepts bullet for `.Include` ("chain onto a LINQ query"), so the one word that places `.Include` is a word I was never taught. Connections even says querying-with-linq holds "the mechanism this lesson relies on", yet nothing told me to read it first.
issues.quote: you know a change tracker keeps entities in memory, and that a query built with LINQ only reaches PostgreSQL once something asks it for results.
issues.fix: Split the Before you start bullet in two and add the lesson that taught LINQ: "[[backend.l1.querying-with-linq]] - you know a LINQ query is how `EfOrderRepository` asks PostgreSQL for rows, and that it only runs when something asks it for results.", leaving the change tracker half on the saving-changes bullet.

issues.text: The correction to the first misconception turns on "lazy loading", which the lesson never defines and which is not a term I know. I cannot tell whether it is something I would have to switch off, something EF Core does somewhere else, or something that would have made the loop version fine after all. Quiz q2's answer depends on the same undefined term.
issues.quote: this codebase has no lazy loading configured, so a different method that returned orders without `.Include(o => o.Customer)` would leave `order.Customer` `null`
issues.fix: Replace "this codebase has no lazy loading configured, so" with "nothing in this project fills `order.Customer` in by itself when you read it, so" - same point, no new term.

issues.text: "the same `DbContext` instance" is a second unknown in that same sentence. saving-changes taught me a change tracker that keeps entities in memory, but not a class called `DbContext`, and not how far one "instance" of it reaches - one request? one method? one run of the app? Without that I cannot judge the escape clause, which is exactly the part that decides whether `order.Customer` is null.
issues.quote: would leave `order.Customer` `null` unless that customer had already been loaded into the same `DbContext` instance, not slow.
issues.fix: Replace "into the same `DbContext` instance" with "by an earlier query in the same request, into the change tracker" - change tracker is a term saving-changes already gave me.
